response.initial_request: The bedroom window has not been closing fully. The handle appears to work, but the window does not seal. The tenant believes the hinges may be the cause and says the window is a standard type. No special access arrangements were reported.

events.body: Reports that a bedroom window will not close or seal fully; handle seems to work and hinges may be at fault. Says the window is standard and there are no special access arrangements.
Sent the tenant's description and asked whether Northbridge Lettings may arrange an inspection and repair.
Sent a concise follow-up asking whether the repair should be arranged by the agency or by the landlord.
Says he is waiting to obtain the insurance excess and asks the agency to call him to discuss when work can proceed.
No connected conversation recorded.
Asks the agency to contact the tenant and find a time for him to visit and inspect the window. Says he has tried calling the agency twice.
Asks when the landlord can visit to inspect the window.
Says someone will be home each day through 26 August and asks whether several calls from an unfamiliar number were from the agency. No number is included in the message.
Relays the tenant's availability through 26 August and asks whether it suits his proposed visit.
Confirms that the tenant's availability works for him.
Forwards an email from a contractor containing an electrical installation condition report.
Updates the tenant that the landlord expects to attend during the available period.

Says nobody has yet inspected the window. The tenant missed two unfamiliar calls while at work and will not call back without a voicemail or message because of scam concerns. Requests that the landlord message first or that the agency coordinate contact. Adds that rain and falling temperatures make the window being partly open a concern.
The landlord says he wants to inspect the window himself before sending a contractor and thinks it may only need lubrication. He offers to attend the following morning between 10:00 and 12:00.
Tenant agrees to be home the following morning between 10:00 and 12:00 for the landlord's proposed inspection.
Confirms the tenant is available the following morning between 10:00 and 12:00. The landlord agrees to attend.
Asks whether the landlord-arranged window work is complete and invites the tenant to report if nobody has attended.
Says a contractor told them parts need to be ordered and that the contractor would contact them the following week.
Forwards an email with an attached Landlord Gas Safety Record. The forwarding email contains no additional message.
Says, “All jobs was done.” The tenant explains they did not notify the agency because Richard, the contractor, said he would send a report.

args.subject: Bedroom window - please confirm it now closes properly
args.body: Hello Elena, thank you for your message. Before we close the request for 24 Bramblewick Lane, Alderfen, ZZ1 1ZZ, could you confirm that the bedroom window now closes and seals fully, and that the hinge parts the contractor needed to order have been fitted? If the window is still not closing properly, please tell us and we will follow it up with the landlord.

args.subject: Bedroom window repair - 24 Bramblewick Lane, Alderfen, ZZ1 1ZZ
args.body: Hello Dorian, the tenant tells us the bedroom window work at 24 Bramblewick Lane, Alderfen, ZZ1 1ZZ is done (the contractor, Richard, is said to be sending a report). Earlier she said parts needed ordering. Could you confirm the window repair is complete, and tell us whether there is any invoice or report we should have on file? Please also note that the gas safety record you forwarded on 10 September relates to a different property, so please resend the correct one if it is meant for this case.

args.reason: Waiting for Tenant and Landlord to confirm the bedroom window repair is complete, before closing.

args.summary: Landlord handled the window repair himself/with his contractor; the tenant says "All jobs was done" but it is unclear that the window itself is fixed. Asked tenant and landlord to confirm completion and follow-up set; not closing yet.
facts: Landlord inspected/arranged his own work (events 14, 16); no agency contractor instructed.
Contractor told tenant parts needed ordering (event 18).
Tenant says 'All jobs was done' and a contractor, Richard, will send a report (event 20).
No invoice or contractor report is on file.
conflicts: Forwarded gas safety record (forwarded-document.pdf, event 19) is for a different property and is irrelevant to the window; event 11 electrical report likewise unrelated.
Event 18 (parts to be ordered) vs event 20 (all jobs done): probably messages crossing in time, but 'all jobs' is vague.
missing: Confirmation the bedroom window now closes and seals
Landlord/contractor confirmation of completion and any invoice or report
options_rejected: Close now: completion is only vaguely stated and nothing confirms the window specifically.
Escalate: no real contradiction; one message to the tenant and landlord can settle it.
Wait only: a direct confirmation is cheap to ask for.
args.uncertainty: Unclear whether 'All jobs' refers to the window or to other jobs such as the electrical and gas paperwork.
